recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which side you would work out first and what the final line has to state.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Work out the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark. Number this answer (1) so the comparison at the end has something to point back to.

recall.must_convey: That A ∩ C = {1, 3, 5} and that adding B gives {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}.
accept: A intersection C is one three five, then union B gives one to five and seven
do the bracket first, intersection then union
left side comes to one two three four five seven
bracket lo intersection mundu cheyyali, taruvatha B union
left hand side is the set one two three four five seven

steps.why: The left side is one intersection followed by one union, so it is the shorter side. Doing it first gives a set to compare the longer side against.
common_mistakes: Writing A ∩ C = {1, 2, 3, 5} and keeping 2, which is in C but not in A.
Keeping 0 in A ∩ C — 0 is in A but not in C.
Writing 1 twice in the union; a set lists each member once.
steps.memory_tip: Do the bracket first: the ∩ is inside the bracket and the ∪ is outside it.

steps.label: Work out the right side and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The word 'show' means the last line must state that the two sides are equal, not just leave two matching sets on the page.

lines.text: ∴ from (1) and (2), (A ∩ C) ∪ B = (A ∪ B) ∩ (C ∪ B)

recall.must_convey: That both unions are formed, their intersection is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}, and the two sides are stated to be equal.
accept: A union B and C union B, then intersect them
the right side also comes to one two three four five seven
both sides are equal so the result is shown
rendu unions teesi intersect cheste same set vasthundi
zero drops out and eight drops out, so the two sides match

steps.why: The two sides come out the same set, which is the distributive law of union over intersection checked on these particular sets. The final line is what earns the mark for a question that says 'show'.
common_mistakes: Keeping 0 in the answer: 0 is in A ∪ B but not in C ∪ B.
Keeping 8 in the answer: 8 is in C ∪ B but not in A ∪ B.
Stopping after the two unions and never taking their intersection.
steps.memory_tip: B is united with both brackets on the right side, so every member of B is in the final set.
